description:
Department/ Unit: Faculty of Law
Closing Date: Until the post is filled
The Faculty of Law at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK LAW) is among the most dynamic and accomplished law schools in Asia. Since welcoming its inaugural cohort in 2006, CUHK LAW has experienced remarkable growth, both in scale and international stature. With a strong global outlook, our academic staff represent nearly twenty jurisdictions through their origins or training.
CUHK LAW is now inviting applications for appointment(s) as Professional Consultant(s). Professional Consultants primarily focus on teaching courses in the Postgraduate Certificate in Laws (PCLL) programme, as well as core and elective common law subjects in the LLB, JD, and LLM programmes.
Applicants should possess: (i) a law degree from a recognized university and/or a relevant professional qualification for legal practice; (ii) at least two years of post-qualification experience as a solicitor or barrister in Hong Kong, or its equivalent in another common law jurisdiction; and (iii) experience in teaching law or demonstrable aptitude for legal education.
Candidates with expertise in the following areas are of particular interest: Writing and Drafting Commercial Documents (English and Chinese), Commercial Practice, China Practice, and Banking and Finance. Applications from highly qualified individuals with other areas of expertise may also be considered.
The appointee(s) will perform duties assigned by the Faculty Dean, including but not limited to: (a) teaching at the CUHK Graduate Law Centre in Central and the CUHK campus in Shatin; (b) contributing to curriculum development and supporting programme administration; (c) serving as academic advisor(s) to students; and (d) undertaking administrative duties and providing service to CUHK LAW, the College, and/or the University, as appropriate.
The appointment(s) will initially be made on a contract basis for up to three years, renewable subject to mutual agreement and satisfactory performance.
Applicants are required to complete the online application form and upload the following documents: a full curriculum vitae; a statement of teaching philosophy and/or methodology (maximum 2 pages); copies of qualification documents; and contact details of three referees who have agreed to provide references. Applicants with current or prior law school teaching experience should also include teaching evaluations. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.
CUHK LAW is firmly committed to fostering diversity and warmly encourages applications from candidates whose backgrounds and experiences will enrich the diversity of our faculty. Further details about CUHK LAW can be found at http://www.cuhk.edu.hk/law .
Applications will be considered on a rolling basis until the relevant teaching needs of the Faculty have been met. We regret that we will only be able to contact candidates selected for further consideration.
The University only accepts and considers applications submitted online for the post above via the CUHK career site. For more information and to apply online, please visit http://career.cuhk.edu.hk .

description:
Department/ Unit: Department of Management
Closing Date: Until the position(s) is/ are filled
The Department of Management at the CUHK Business School is now inviting applications for faculty position(s) at the Professor/ Associate Professor levels commencing in 202 7 . Applications are invited from qualified scholars with expertise in macro management (e.g., strategy, innovation, entrepreneurship, international business, family business, sustainability, etc.) or micro management (e.g., organizational behavior, leadership, human resource management, etc.).
Applicants should possess (i) a PhD degree in management or a related discipline; (ii) excellent teaching performance, particularly in delivering graduate courses; (iii) a sound track record of publications in top-tier journals; and (iv) strong commitment to service at Faculty and Departmental levels. The appointee(s) will teach courses mainly at the graduate level, such as MBA, EMBA, DBA and MSc courses; publish high-quality scholarly research; and participate in academic and professional activities. He/she is expected to actively bid for competitive external funding support for research endeavors.
Appointment will commence in 202 7 . Appointment will normally be made on contract basis for up to three years initially, which, subject to mutual agreement, may lead to longer-term appointment or substantiation.
Salary and Fringe Benefits
Salary will be highly competitive, commensurate with qualifications and experience. The University offers a comprehensive fringe benefit package, including medical care and housing benefits for eligible appointee(s).
About the Department of Management
The Department of Management offers three specialized concentrations in Entrepreneurship (ENT), Human Resource Management (HRM), and Management of International Business (MIB) in the Integrated BBA Programme, and two Master’s Programmes in Management and Sustainable Global Business. Our competitive curriculum equips students with cutting-edge knowledge in management, a global outlook, an innovative spirit, and a strong sense of social responsibility and integrity, enabling future business leaders to lead transformative initiatives worldwide. For more information about the Department, please visit our website at https://www.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/departments/management/ .
About CUHK Business School
The CUHK Business School is a leading business school and a pioneer in business education in Hong Kong. Since its establishment in Hong Kong in 1963, the CUHK Business School has gained world recognition of nurturing business leaders with immense contributions in the Asia Pacific.
The Business School has been offering a comprehensive range of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes (MBA, MSc, MAcc, EMBA, DBA, MPhil, PhD) with over 6,500 students from 30+ countries/regions, as well as executive education programmes. It has one of the most extensive alumni networks in the region, with over 4 9 ,000 alumni around the world. It comprises two Schools and four Departments:
Schools
- Accountancy
- Hotel & Tourism Management
Departments
- Finance
- Decisions, Operations and Technology
- Management
- Marketing
Application Procedure
Applicants should submit the application package online via the CUHK career site (including a completed on-line application form, full resume, publication list, and evidence of teaching excellence, if any), and provide names and email addresses of at least three referees for providing reference.
The University only accepts and considers applications submitted online for the post above via the CUHK career site. For more information and to apply online, please visit http://career.cuhk.edu.hk .
Review of applications will be conducted on a rolling basis and will continue until the position(s) is/are filled. For enquiries, please contact the Department of Management via mgt@cuhk.edu.hk .
Interested scholars are welcome to connect with Department colleagues at upcoming major conferences to learn more about the Department. These include the 2026 AOM Conference (Philadelphia, US), the Department’s AOM Reception (Philadelphia Marriott Downtown, evening of 2 August), and the 2026 AIB Conference (Manchester, UK).

The Department of Curriculum and Instruction under the Faculty of Education at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is a dynamic centre in the Asia-Pacific region for teaching and research in the broad areas of curriculum and instruction. In addition to Faculty-based undergraduate teacher education, Postgraduate Diploma in Education, Master of Education, Doctor of Education and PhD programmes, the Department offers several Master of Arts/ Science programmes as well as research supervision across a range of subject areas. The Faculty of Education of CUHK is an international centre for professional training and research in education. Detailed information about the Faculty of Education and the Department is available at http://www.fed.cuhk.edu.hk/ .
The Department invites applications for a full-time appointment as Senior Lecturer/ Lecturer in Curriculum Studies.
For Senior Lecturer, applicants should have (i) a relevant doctoral degree; and (ii) at least 8 years of post-doctoral relevant experience. Evidence of research and scholarly activities is also generally expected.
For Lecturer, applicants should have (i) a Master’s degree (preferably a doctoral degree in a relevant discipline); and (ii) at least 4 years of post-Master relevant experience. Applicants who possess a doctoral degree with less experience will also be considered.

A good track record of pedagogical research and an initial record of refereed publications are added advantages.

The Department of Electronic Engineering (EE) at the Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is seeking outstanding candidates for Research Assistant Professorship (RAP).

The research focuses on advancing neuromorphic/physical computing, optical signal processing, integrated photonics. (i) a PhD in Electronic Engineering, Optoelectronic Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related discipline;
(ii) a strong track record of research and publications in reputable journals and conferences;
(iii) excellent communication and interpersonal skills;
(iv) potential to become an independent researcher in obtaining future/sustained extramural funding and establishing significant externally-funded research programmes;
The appointee will work closely with Prof. Chaoran Huang in the Department to enhance the existing strengths. The appointee is expected to:
(a) be able to have top-tier research outputs and apply for RGC GRF grants and similar external competitive grants;
(b) undertake some teaching duties at undergraduate and postgraduate levels; and
(c) provide service at departmental, faculty and/or university levels.

To apply, please upload a full resume, copies of academic credentials, a publication list with soft copies of the five most representative publications, details of courses taught and evaluation results (if available), a research plan, a teaching statement, and the names and contact information of three to five referees.
Appointment will initially be made on contract basis for up to three years, renewable subject to performance, funding availability and mutual agreement. description:
Department/ Unit: Zhizhen School of Interdisciplinary Mathematical Sciences
Closing date: Until the posts are filled
Founded in 1963, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is a forward-looking comprehensive research university with a global vision and a mission to combine tradition with modernity, and to bring together China and the West.
CUHK has established the Zhizhen School of Interdisciplinary Mathematical Sciences ("Zhizhen School" or "the School"). It aims to cultivate mathematical science talent in Hong Kong, aligning with the national aspiration to building China into a leading country in education, as well as the 14th Five-Year Plan’s vision of strengthening basic research. This also aligns with the aspiration in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region government’s policy address to develop Hong Kong as an international hub for post-secondary education and establish the “Study in Hong Kong” brand. Professor Shing-tung Yau is the Founding Director of Zhizhen School.
The School will offer an eight-year training programme similar to that of Qiuzhen College in Tsinghua University which includes three years of mathematical foundation training, two years of scientific research training and three years of doctoral training. Students who fulfil the general academic and whole-person education graduation requirements will be awarded CUHK Bachelor and PhD degrees. The School will build a team of world-class scholars, who will participate in high-level scientific research, lead various academic activities of the School, and also be responsible for teaching and supervising students and postdoctoral fellows.
The School is now inviting applications for substantiable-track faculty posts at all the academic levels.
Applicants should have (i) a relevant PhD degree in mathematics or related disciplines; (ii) an established track record in research, including publications; and (iii) a demonstrated commitment to excellence in teaching.
Appointments will normally be made on contract basis for up to three years initially commencing August 2025, which, subject to mutual agreement, may lead to substantiation or longer-term appointment later.
Applicants please upload a full resume and attach copies of academic credentials, together with names and e-mail addresses of three to five referees (at least two on research and one on teaching) to whom the applicants' consent has been given for their providing references.
Review of applications will begin on May 15, 2025, and will continue until the positions are filled.

Department/ Unit: Department of Translation
Closing date: October 31, 2026
Established in 1972, the Department of Translation of CUHK was the first of its kind in Asia. We offer a full range of BA, MA, MPhil and PhD programmes.
As a historic leader in translation studies, our department is dedicated to shaping the future of a discipline in transition. Building on our robust foundation in humanities research, we aim to pioneer new approaches at the intersection of language, culture, and technology. We are currently expanding our vision beyond traditional, practical translation training, with the goal of leading the global conversation on digital multilingualism and the cultural impact of emerging language technologies.
We are seeking forward-thinking scholars who possess a strong foundation in humanities research and who have (or are highly motivated to develop) an active engagement with emerging technologies. We are particularly interested in candidates whose work critically engages with how language, technology, and society intersect. Relevant areas of expertise reflect this synthesis of humanities and technology, and include, but are not limited to: AI and translation and interpreting technologies; audiovisual translation and multimodal translation; localization; and multilingual digital communication.
While priority will be given to the areas listed above, applicants in all areas of translation studies who demonstrate a commitment to integrating technology and culture into their research and teaching are welcome to apply.
Applicants should (i) possess a PhD degree in translation or other related fields; (ii) have relevant teaching experience and professional qualification(s); and (iii) possess a strong track record in publishing research in the field. The appointees will be expected to (a) teach undergraduate and/or postgraduate courses; (b) develop new courses in line with their own interests; (c) supervise research postgraduate students; (d) develop independent and/or collaborative research projects; and (e) undertake administrative duties.
A complete application dossier should include (a) a cover letter, indicating the rank and mode of appointment you are applying for; (b) a CV, with a complete list of publications (attach the acceptance letter for an accepted but unpublished paper); (c) a research statement; (d) a teaching statement; (e) two writing samples, published or unpublished; (f) previous teaching evaluations if any; and (g) applications for assistant professors should have three confidential reference letters to be sent by the referees directly; (h) associate professor applications should include three names of referees. Established in 1998, the School of Hotel and Tourism Management is one of six departments within the CUHK Business School. Leveraging the Business School's esteemed business education, the school is dedicated to developing future leaders in the experience economy, with a focus on hospitality, tourism, and real estate. The school provides an AACSB-accredited BBA program in Hospitality and Real Estate (HRE), the first integrated undergraduate program of its kind in Asia. At the postgraduate level, it offers two MSc programmes. The MSc in Real Estate (MRE) is the only master's degree in Asia that integrates multidisciplinary research and teaching from real estate, business, and hospitality and the MSc in Leadership for Experience Economy (LEE) is the first MSc programme in the Asia-Pacific region focusing on developing competencies in inspirational leadership, investment, and innovation to drive organizational success in the emerging experience economy. The CUHK Business School is a leading business school and a pioneer in business education in Hong Kong. Since its establishment in Hong Kong in 1963, the CUHK Business School has gained world recognition of nurturing business leaders with immense contributions in Asia Pacific. The School has been offering a comprehensive range of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes with over 6,500 students from 30+ countries/regions, as well as executive education. description:
Department/ Unit: Department of Biomedical Engineering
Closing Date: June 1, 2027
The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is a widely accepted top institute in Asia (e.g. ranked #7 in QS Asia University Rankings 2026) with a high degree of global academic reputation (e.g. ranked #18 in QS World University Rankings 2027). The Faculty of Engineering at CUHK is famous for its research in optics and photonics, dating back to the early 1970s when Prof Charles Kao (2009 Nobel Laureate in Physics) joined CUHK.
The Department of Biomedical Engineering (BME) is the newest in the Faculty of Engineering. Still, it has already grown into global academic excellence (world #38 in 2025 Shanghai Ranking of Academic Subjects – Biomedical Engineering) and is consistently ranked No. 1 in Hong Kong. We are inviting applications for the post of Research Assistant Professor (RAP) in BME to engage in a project related to glycosaminoglycan-rich biomaterials for musculoskeletal tissue engineering applications. The project is highly interdisciplinary, involving areas of biomaterials, extracellular matrix, stem cells, mechanoregulation and musculoskeletal disorders.
Opportunities for Growth
The RAP position offers great opportunities for professional development, including leading independent cutting-edge research projects, mentoring postdocs and graduate students, collaborating with world-leading research groups, applying for grants and classroom teaching.
Requirements
Applicants should (i) possess a doctoral degree in the STEM field, such as biomedical engineering, mechanical engineering, computer engineering and applied physics; (ii) have a solid academic background in biomaterials, extracellular matrix, musculoskeletal tissue engineering and an excellent research track record; (iii) demonstrate a strong academic track record as evidenced by publishing in high-profile journals or conferences; and (iv) have proficiency in both written and spoken English. Solid postdoctoral training on carbohydrate materials is essential, but applicants with exceptional research achievements will be considered case-by-case. Experience in leading research projects independently is required, and success in research grant applications will be considered an advantage.
Research Directions
The RAP position is dedicated to working and developing glycosaminoglycan-rich biomaterials for musculoskeletal applications. This project is based on our prior foundation of complex extracellular matrix biomaterials for tissue engineering. Through the already-established collaboration, this study will pave the way for upcoming clinical translation in musculoskeletal tissue engineering and support the translation of Hong Kong’s scientific excellence into societal impacts. The specific aims and deliverables of research projects will be discussed with the PI, considering the applicant’s expertise, interests, and prior experience.
Responsibilities
The appointee’s roles and contributions include: (a) carry on the proposed project under the lead of the PI (Prof. CHAN Barbara): specifically, the appointee will (i) coordinate the GAG-rich biomaterial program; (ii) assist in mentoring RPg students working on the project; (iii) collaborate with biologists/clinicians to explore broad applications of the project; and (iv) prepare conference/journal manuscripts and drafting patents; (b) generate high-impact research outputs that are equivalent to the 4* research output in RAE: the appointee is expected to have cross-field working experience to support the multidisciplinary nature of this project; and (c) apply for external grants from RGC/NSFC/ITC/etc.: the appointee will be fostered to be an independent researcher with a good track record of securing external grants. The research results from this project are expected to strongly support the appointee in applying for and securing external grants.
Salary and Contract Details
Salary will be commensurate with the applicant’s qualifications and experience. Appointment will initially be made on contract basis for up to three years, starting as soon as possible, renewable subject to funding availability, performance and mutual agreement.
How to Apply
Applicants should submit an online application and attach a full resume, a list of publications, copies of academic credentials, together with names, addresses and e-mail addresses of three to five referees to whom the applicants' consent has been given for their providing references. The review of applications will begin immediately and will continue until the positions are filled. Only shortlisted applicants will be notified.
The University only accepts and considers applications submitted online for the post above via the CUHK career site. For more information and to apply online, please visit http://career.cuhk.edu.hk .

Department of Social Work
Associate Professor
(Ref. 250000U3) ( Closing Date: Until the post (s) is / are filled .)
As a world-leading centre of social work education and research, the Department is dedicated to developing and disseminating scientific rigorous and socially impactful social work knowledge for human betterment and social development. We aspire, through our research and evaluation work, to improve the lives of vulnerable and disadvantaged groups, deepen our understanding of social issues and promote evidence-based practice locally and globally. The Department is looking for candidates who embrace these goals and values.
Scholars specializing in any of the following research areas are welcome to apply for the post s :
- clinical social work
- children and family
- gerontology
- macro social work theories and practice
Applicants should have (i) a relevant PhD degree; (ii) a strong publication track record; (iii) proven ability to obtain grants and conduct research to generate academic and social impact; (iv) demonstrated academic leadership; and (v) evidence of outstanding teaching performance. Being registered social workers and having professional expertise or substantial work experience in clinical or macro social work practice will be added assets.
The appointees will ( a ) undertake research; ( b ) teach undergraduate and postgraduate courses; ( c ) supervise research postgraduate students; and ( d ) take up key administrative roles for the Department.
Appointments will normally be made on contract basis for up to three years initially, which, subject to mutual agreement, may lead to longer-term appointment or substantiation.
Application Procedure
The University only accepts and considers applications submitted online for the post via the CUHK career site. For more information and to apply online, please visit http://career.cuhk.edu.hk .

Department/ Unit: School of Hotel and Tourism Management
Closing date: January 15, 2027
The School of Hotel and Tourism Management at the Business School of the Chinese University of Hong Kong is inviting applications for a tenure-track faculty position in hospitality and tourism, starting in August 2027.
Applicants should be promising scholars with a PhD (by the time of reporting for duty) in hospitality and tourism or a related field. The appointees will conduct high quality research which results in publications in top-tier hospitality and tourism journals. In addition, they are expected to undertake duties to teach basic and advanced-level hospitality and tourism courses at both undergraduate and/or postgraduate levels, and to render services to the School of Hotel and Tourism Management. We welcome applications from scholars specializing in AI and machine learning, behavioral science, healthcare and aging, sports and entertainment, and related areas. Industry experience in related fields and/or grant experience is preferred.
Appointment will normally be made on contract basis for up to three years initially commencing August 2027, which, subject to demonstration of the requisite level of performance and mutual agreement, may lead to a longer-term appointment or substantiation later.
About the School of Hotel and Tourism Management
Established in 1998, the School of Hotel and Tourism Management is one of six departments within the CUHK Business School. Leveraging the Business School's esteemed business education, the school is dedicated to developing future leaders in the experience economy, with a focus on hospitality, tourism, and real estate. The school provides an AACSB-accredited BBA program in Hospitality and Real Estate (HRE), the first integrated undergraduate program of its kind in Asia. At the postgraduate level, it offers two MSc programmes. The MSc in Real Estate (MRE) is the only master's degree in Asia that integrates multidisciplinary research and teaching from real estate, business, and hospitality and the MSc in Leadership for Experience Economy (LEE) is the first MSc programme in the Asia-Pacific region focusing on developing competencies in inspirational leadership, investment, and innovation to drive organizational success in the emerging experience economy. In addition, the school offers the MPhil-PhD in Business Administration, specializing in Hospitality and Real Estate, preparing students for academic and research careers.
Further information about the School of Hotel and Tourism Management is available at https://www.bschool.cuhk.edu.hk/departments/hotel-and-tourism-management/
About CUHK Business School
The CUHK Business School is a leading business school and a pioneer in business education in Hong Kong. Since its establishment in Hong Kong in 1963, the CUHK Business School has gained world recognition of nurturing business leaders with immense contributions in Asia Pacific. The School has been offering a comprehensive range of undergraduate and postgraduate programmes with over 6,500 students from 30+ countries/regions, as well as executive education. It has one of the most extensive alumni networks in the region, with over 49,000 alumni around the world. It comprises two Schools and four Departments:

· Accountancy

Departments
· Decisions, Operations and Technology
· Finance
· Management
· Marketing

Department of History
Assistant Professor (Public History)
(Ref. 260001AK) (Closing Date: October 1, 2026)
The Department of History at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) invites applications for a full-time, substantiation-track ( equivalent to U.S. tenure-track) position at the rank of Assistant Professor in the field of Public History, begin ning August 2, 2027.
CUHK’s History Department is proud to have been the first department in the region to offer an MA in Comparative and Public History, and we have recently added a unique undergraduate stream in Public History. We seek a dynamic scholar-practitioner whose work engages with both public and scholarly audiences in innovative ways. The successful candidate will be expected to teach an introductory methodology course in Public History. In addition, their research and practice should evince a dedication to meaningful engagement with the community, governmental and non-governmental organizations, etc. (either in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region of the People’s Republic of China or elsewhere). A track record (appropriate to career stage) of scholarly publication is expected.
We welcome applicants with specialisations in any area of Public History, including (but not limited to):
· Museum and heritage studies
· Oral history
· Community-engaged history
· Digital public history
· Archival and curatorial practice
· Historical memory and commemoration
Experience in Digital Humanities (DH) and innovative public-facing methodologies is highly desirable. The position is open to all qualified candidates, both local and international. The normal teaching load is two courses per term, reduced to one in the first term of appointment. Teaching will be conducted in English, although knowledge of Chinese will be considered an advantage.
Qualifications:
Applicants should:
i . h old a PhD in History or a closely related field by August 1, 202 7;
ii . h ave an active research agenda with clear plans for future publications ;
iii . d emonstrate a commitment to teaching and mentoring students ; and
iv . s how evidence of public history practice and engagement (including evidence of social impact, where appropriate) .
Salary and fringe benefits for the post will be highly competitive. Appointment will normally be made on a contract basis for up to three years initially , which, subject to funding, performance and mutual agreement, may lead to longer-term appointment or substantiation (equivalent to U.S. tenure), either after six years of service or earlier upon special application and recommendation.
Application Process
Applicants should complete the online application form, upload a letter of introduction, a CV, evidence of public history practice and/or engagement with the community and one writing sample. Review of applications will begin on October 1, 2026 and continue until the position is filled. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to provide further materials, including letters of recommendation (to be addressed to the Department Secretary directly by the referees), evidence of teaching and public engagement experience.
The University only accepts and considers applications submitted online for the post above via the CUHK career site. For more information and to apply online, please visit http://career.cuhk.edu.hk .

Department of History
Assistant Professor (Ancient World History)
(Ref. 260001AJ ) (Closing Date: October 1, 2026)
The Department of History at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) invites applications for a full-time, substantiation-track position at the rank of Assistant Professor in the field of Ancient World History, begin ning August 2, 2027. We welcome applicants with specialisations in areas including (but not limited to) ancient Europe, North Africa, the Middle East, and the Mediterranean world in the period c. 1000 BCE–500 CE. While chronological and thematic specialisations are open, the ability to teach ancient Greek and/or Roman history is highly desirable. The post is open to all qualified candidates, both local and international.
CUHK is one of Asia’s top international research universities, ranked number #18 globally in 2027 by QS and #44 by THE . Our department has the largest cluster of World History expertise in Hong Kong and the wider region. We hope to recruit a historian who can complement and expand our existing subject coverage, helping us achieve our goal of becoming Asia’s leading centre for the study of World History. The primary language of research and instruction in World History at CUHK is English; knowledge of Chinese is not required.
The successful candidate will have a strong commitment to high standards in both research and teaching. An active research agenda and clear plans for future English-language publications (including a monograph and peer-reviewed journal articles) are essential. In addition to delivering the department’s introductory survey course on Ancient World History (HIST2005), a key responsibility will be to further develop the World History curriculum, by creating new courses in line with the candidate’s interests and the department’s needs. The normal teaching load is two courses per term, reduced to one course in the first term of employment.
Qualifications
Applicants should:
i . have obtained a doctoral degree by August 1, 2027;
ii . have an active research agenda and clear plans for future English-language publications;
iii . be committed to teaching at both undergraduate and postgraduate levels; and
iv . be ready to supervise postgraduate students.
Salary and fringe benefits for the post will be highly competitive. Appointment will normally be made on a contract basis for up to three years initially, which may be renewed for a further three years. Subject to funding, performance, and mutual agreement, this may lead to longer-term appointment or substantiation (equivalent to U.S. tenure), either when the aggregate service period reaches six years, or sooner upon completing one year’s service, subject to special application and recommendation as appropriate.

Review of applications will begin on October 1, 2026 and continue until the position is filled. Shortlisted candidates will be asked to provide further materials, including letters of recommendation (to be addressed to the Department Secretary directly by the referees) and evidence of experience as both researchers and teachers.

description:
Department/ Unit: Faculty of Law
Closing Date: September 15, 2026
The Faculty of Law of The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK LAW) is one of the most dynamic and accomplished research-intensive law schools in Asia. Since welcoming its inaugural student cohort in 2006, CUHK LAW has earned international recognition for excellence in legal research and education. This reputation is affirmed by the latest Research Assessment Exercise (2020) conducted by Hong Kong’s University Grants Committee, in which 83% of the Faculty’s research output was rated as “world-leading” (4*) or “internationally excellent” (3*). With a strong global outlook, our academic staff represent nearly twenty jurisdictions through their origins or training.
CUHK LAW now invites applications for appointment as Professor, Associate Professor, or Assistant Professor. The Faculty upholds a robust and ambitious research culture, with research excellence firmly at the core of its academic mission. We place particular emphasis on high-quality scholarship that advances disciplinary debates and contributes meaningfully to global and regional conversations in law.
Candidates for appointment at the Professor level are expected to have an established record of academic leadership in research and/or education at the international level. They should demonstrate a sustained trajectory of influential scholarship and a proven ability to mentor colleagues in advancing the Faculty’s research profile. Appointees at the Associate Professor level should have an internationally recognised reputation for research excellence and a proven capacity to contribute to the Faculty’s research profile. Candidates at this level should already possess a strong portfolio of high-impact publications and a clear scholarly agenda of continuing distinction. Candidates for Assistant Professorships should have completed their doctorate by the time of appointment and either possess a strong record of quality publications or demonstrate clear potential to develop into a productive and impactful scholar. Clear evidence of a coherent research trajectory and commitment to producing high-quality outputs will be essential.
The Faculty particularly welcomes applications in foundational common law subjects (especially private law subjects), artificial intelligence and law, intellectual property law, and PRC law. Exceptionally well-qualified candidates in other areas may also be considered.
Applicants should complete the online application form and upload the following documents:
(a) a cover letter (maximum 2 pages);
(b) a full curriculum vitae;
(c) a teaching statement (maximum 2 pages); and
(d) a statement of major research and scholarly achievements (maximum 3 pages), highlighting up to four representative publications or research outputs from the past five years, with a description of their originality, significance, and rigour.
Appointments will normally be made on contract basis of up to three years initially, which, subject to mutual agreement, may lead to longer-term appointment or substantiation.
The current starting base salary, payable over 12 months, is HK$80,825 per month (approximately US$10,350 / £7,800 per month) for Assistant Professors; HK$100,050 per month (approximately US$12,825 / £9,650 per month) for Associate Professors; and HK$126,370 per month (approximately US$16,200 / £12,190 per month) for Professors. In addition to the base salary, appointees are eligible for a monthly housing allowance and an end-of-contract gratuity, subject to prevailing terms and conditions.
CUHK LAW is committed to promoting diversity and warmly welcomes applications from candidates whose backgrounds and experiences will enrich the intellectual and cultural life of the Faculty. Further information about CUHK LAW is available at http://www.cuhk.edu.hk/law .
The application deadline is 15 September 2026, and applications will be considered on a rolling basis. We regret that we will only be able to contact candidates selected for further consideration.
Prospective applicants are welcome to contact the Dean of the Faculty at deanoflaw@cuhk.edu.hk for informal inquiries.
The University only accepts and considers applications submitted online for the post above via the CUHK career site. For more information and to apply online, please visit http://career.cuhk.edu.hk .

Founded in 1963, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is a forward-looking comprehensive research university with a global vision and a mission to combine tradition with modernity, and to bring together China and the West. We seek promising young mathematicians whose research areas match the areas of our faculty members. Applicants should have (i) a PhD degree in mathematics or related disciplines; and (ii) demonstrated potential for research and teaching. The main duties of the appointees will focus on research. Applicants please upload a full resume and attach copies of academic credentials, together with names and e-mail addresses of at least four referees (at least three on research and one on teaching) to whom the applicants' consent has been given for their providing references. The School is seeking outstanding candidates, early career or established social scientists, with expertise in the area of AI and computational communication, to join the expanding faculty team as Professor / Associate Professor/ Assistant Professor. Faculty members are productive and committed researchers as well as devoted educators. The faculty team at the School features a combination of highly promising young scholars and established scholars who are leaders in their own fields, including two elected Fellows of the International Communication Association. Chair Professor / Professor / Professor of Practice and Director (25260536)
Overview
The Academy of Film is a leading force in cinematic and creative media education, with aspirations that extend well beyond Hong Kong’s local film market. Its influence is reflected in the achievements of its respected faculty—many of whom are distinguished filmmakers and scholars —and its alumni, who are recognised across Asia and beyond. In recent years, the Academy has furthered its global engagement through initiatives such as the Global University Film Awards, which have garnered significant international attention and participation. State-of-the-art facilities support this vision, including the recent installation of two world-class virtual production studios, ensuring students and faculty work at the cutting edge of industry practice. Supported by strong industry connections and a commitment to excellence, the Academy of Film continues to cultivate talent equipped for the global screen industries. Established as the Department of Cinema and Television in 1991, today’s Academy of Film has grown into a leading hub for screen and media education. Renamed in 2009 to reflect its broader ambitions, the Academy is now part of the School of Creative Arts alongside the Academy of Music and Academy of Visual Arts, supporting a multidisciplinary approach that extends to art-tech and global entertainment business. Energised by innovation and driven by a spirit of creative exchange, the Academy of Film is a place for makers and thinkers ready to push boundaries and shape the future of screen arts.

The Academy of Film seeks an inspiring, visionary Director to lead the school at the intersection of traditional film scholarships and the rapidly evolving landscape of film and media production. Working to advance scholarship, promote creative and artistic accomplishment, education and civic engagement, and encourage distinctive curricular design and development, the Director fosters a collaborative, inclusive environment that supports faculty research and secures inspiring, future-focused learning experiences for students. A vital element of the role is forging and deepening partnerships with filmmakers, studios, and technology leaders across the creative industries, ensuring engagement with current industry trends and real-world projects.
Supporting the University’s research mission, the Director will advance the faculty’s scholarly activities, including opportunities afforded by interdisciplinary approaches. The Director serves as the Academy’s public voice, articulating its contributions to local, state, regional, cross-border and international communities.
Ideal candidates will be recognised for scholarly and/or professional achievement, with demonstrated leadership and administrative experience in a creative environment and academia, and a strong commitment to education and scholarship. The Director manages a large number of academic and administrative staff across Film/TV, Acting for Global Screen, MA in Producing, MFA in Film Production, and PhD studies.

description:
Full-time/Part-time Research Assistant I / Senior Research Assistant
Research Assistant I / Senior Research Assistant in the Faculty of Law (Ref.:537320) (to commence as soon as possible, on a three-month temporary basis)
The appointee will work on a project involving quantitative and socio‑legal analysis of approximately 2,300+ drug trafficking sentencing judgments from the Hong Kong High Court and District Court, and the preparation of an in‑depth report on drug trafficking trends and sentencing patterns for an NGO partner serving youth offenders.
Applicants should possess a Master’s degree or above in socio‑legal studies, Social Work, Criminology, Statistics / Data Science, Public Policy / Social Policy, or a closely related field with substantial quantitative methods training. They should have:
Training in descriptive statistics, inferential analysis, and data visualisation
Ability to work with structured datasets (e.g. CSV/Excel)
Competence in at least one data analysis environment (e.g. R, Python, Stata, SPSS, or similar)
Demonstrated ability to write clear, structured, analytical reports in English
Ability to interpret and synthesise complex information (including legal judgments and social data)
Good organisational skills and ability to work independently to meet deadlines
A law degree or legal training is an advantage, especially if combined with quantitative skills, but is not a substitute for the quantitative methods requirement.
The appointee’s primary task will be to lead the analysis and writing of an in‑depth report, including:
Analysing an existing dataset of coded drug trafficking sentencing judgments (approx. 2,300+ cases)
Conducting descriptive and inferential quantitative analysis (e.g. regression, group comparisons, trends over time)
Identifying trends and patterns in:
Case background (time, place, court level; high‑risk periods/locations)
Defendant characteristics (age, gender, nationality, education, occupation, family structure, health/addiction, prior records)
Trafficking behaviours (drug type/weight, trafficking methods, motives, financial benefits)

description:
The Division of Landscape Architecture, Department of Architecture invites applications for Senior Research Assistant / Research Assistant I/II in AI‑Curated Multilingual Visual Glossary for Architecture and Heritage (Ref. no.: 537323). Appointments will commence as soon as possible for 6 to 12 months, full‑time or part‑time, with the possibility of renewal based on performance and funding availability.
This position supports the Teaching Development Grant project “Bridging Linguistic and Conceptual Divides”, which is developing an AI‑curated, multilingual visual glossary and digital library for architectural and heritage conservation terminology in English, Mandarin (Simplified), and Cantonese (Traditional).
2. RESPONSIBILITIES
Depending on experience and appointment level, the appointee will:
Develop and maintain AI-assisted workflows for extracting, organizing, translating, and aligning architectural and heritage terminology from English and Chinese sources.
Use current AI and coding tools, such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or comparable tools, to support research, data processing, prototyping, testing, and documentation.
Build or support practical NLP and retrieval workflows using embeddings, semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation, and related techniques.
Curate multilingual datasets, including Simplified/Traditional Chinese conversion, terminology normalization, metadata, source documentation, and copyright records.
Test AI-generated outputs, identify errors, and prepare materials for validation by academic and professional experts.
Support the development of a web-based visual glossary prototype, including links between terminology, definitions, images, drawings, maps, and other relevant materials.
Work with an interdisciplinary team and document methods, decisions, and project progress clearly.
3. REQUIREMENTS
Applicants should have a Bachelor’s degree or above in any discipline. Appointment at Senior Research Assistant, Research Assistant I, or Research Assistant II level will depend on qualifications and relevant experience.
Applicants should have:
Some practical experience with Python, data processing, NLP, web development, or a related technical area, or clear evidence of the ability to learn these skills quickly.
Experience using current AI tools for research, coding, data analysis, or problem-solving.
Strong reading ability in Simplified and Traditional Chinese, sufficient for working with academic, policy, architectural, and heritage-related materials.
Good written English and the ability to prepare clear research and technical documentation.
Careful attention to data quality, source verification, copyright, and the limitations of AI-generated outputs.
The ability to work independently, meet project milestones, and collaborate with an interdisciplinary team.
For the Senior Research Assistant rank, stronger technical experience and the ability to lead parts of the AI workflow would be expected.
Preferred, but not required:
Experience with advanced AI coding tools such as Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, or comparable agentic coding environments.
Familiarity with embeddings, semantic search, RAG, tool calling, agentic workflows, MCP, or evaluation of AI-generated outputs.
Experience with Chinese NLP, OCR, document AI, multimodal models, knowledge graphs, or large text corpora.
Experience with web frameworks such as Streamlit, FastAPI, Flask, Django, or Next.js.
Familiarity with Cantonese or Hong Kong terminology.
An interest in architecture, landscape, urban planning, heritage conservation, or digital humanities.
How to Apply
Applications are accepted exclusively online. Applicants should submit their application via the University’s Careers site, including an up‑to‑date curriculum vitae (C.V.), relevant examples of their work and a cover letter. Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until 9 October 2026, or until the positions are filled, whichever comes first.

description:
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) invites applications from exceptional candidates for biomedical sciences faculty positions (Professor / Associate Professor / Assistant Professor) for its new School of Medicine.
The University
HKUST is a dynamic young University with a global reputation for impact and innovation. Founded in 1991, HKUST is consistently ranked among the world’s best institutions and 1st in Hong Kong for graduate employability.
As a world-renowned international research and interdisciplinary University with top-tier programs in science, engineering, business and management, humanities and social science, and interdisciplinary studies, HKUST is known for its entrepreneurial culture and powerful connections to industry and research. The University’s English-speaking academic community thrives in a world-class, scenic environment at the Clear Water Bay campus.
HKUST’s pioneering spirit is amplified through the “Unified HKUST, Complementary Campuses” framework, expanded by the opening of the innovative HKUST(Guangzhou) campus in 2022, which deepens its interdisciplinary reach into the Greater Bay Area and beyond.
For more information about HKUST, please visit: https://hkust.edu.hk .
The HKUST School of Medicine
HKUST is embarking on a landmark initiative to establish the third medical school of Hong Kong following the successful proposal of the University and subsequent official approval from the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region Government.
The HKUST School of Medicine aspires to be a transformative force, focused on world-class education and research while attracting global talents. By integrating cutting-edge technology and pioneering science, the School will help shape the future of medicine and reinforce Hong Kong’s position as an international hub for medical training, research, and innovation.
Built upon HKUST’s interdisciplinary strengths, deeply international character, and global networks, the School will foster a world-class learning environment. As a leader in fields such as artificial intelligence, data science, and robotics, HKUST is uniquely positioned to create a medical school that fuses exceptional clinical expertise with technological innovation. description:
HKUST Strategic Hiring 2023
Faculty Positions
( https://hkust.edu.hk/ )
Established in 1991, The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) is a globally recognized University and contributes both locally and internationally to talent development, new knowledge generation and societal interests. The University was founded on the principle that education, original scholarship, and the development of society are integrally linked and best pursued together. It has the objective of becoming a world leading University with significant international impact and strong local commitment. In relentless pursuit of excellence, it leads the advance of and education in science, technology, business, humanities and social science.
Celebrating its 30 th birthday during the most challenging time in the recent decade with mounting global issues of the coronavirus, economic downturn and climate change, the University sees a growing demand for pressing solutions to respond to these emerging challenges. To address these and other global issues, it is essential to bring to the University a diversity of talents and open up new horizons in high-impact areas. One of the objectives in HKUST Strategic Plan 2021-2028 ( https://strategicplan.hkust.edu.hk/ ) is to be “A University of TALENTS”, extending our global reservoir of minds and abilities by looking beyond conventional academic disciplines and being open to the recruitment and nurturing of more diverse areas of strength among students, faculty and staff. Concurring with this objective, the University will conduct a strategic hiring campaign aimed at advancing the University’s academic strengths in selected cross-disciplinary areas that are strategically important to HKUST’s future development. We are seeking renowned scholars, academics, leaders or potential leaders in the core cross-disciplinary areas of (A) Biomedical Science and Translational Medicine ; (B) Material Science and Future Energy ; (C) AI, Future Computing and Electronics ; (D) Innovation for Business Management and FinTech ; (E) Environmental Science, Sustainability and Green Tech ; and (F) Art Tech and Humanities .
Applications are invited for a number of senior substantiation-track faculty positions at the rank of Professor or Associate Professor in the above areas. Joint appointments in more than one academic department in the University are encouraged . Successful candidates should have a PhD degree in related fields and preferably have demonstrated a solid research track record in the above areas. Apart from having an exceptional research record, successful candidates should demonstrate strong potential as excellent teachers and advisors. Good ability in communicating research problems well beyond one’s own research area, especially with organizations and industry partners, is considered a plus.
Appointments can start as early as on 1 June 2023. Salary is highly competitive and will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Fringe benefits include medical/dental benefits, annual leave, and housing benefits where applicable.
Details of the six core cross-disciplinary areas (A) to (F) are as follows:
(A) Biomedical Science and Translational Medicine
Building on the current strength in biological sciences and translational medicine, the University aims to further enhance the research and educational capacity in this important area to address the pressing health issues locally and worldwide. We are seeking motivated scientists who share the same vision and aim to transform medicine using advanced multi-omics diagnosis, AI-driven preventive medicine data analytics, advanced imaging and data integration, precision medicine by gene editing or advanced therapies, or other advanced approaches that provide important insights into disease mechanisms. The candidate will provide leadership in research and teaching in the general area of biomedical sciences with a clear path to translate pre-clinical research into clinical trials and experimental medicine efforts. The candidate will also be expected to develop new research links with internal units and external partners at the interface between medicine and industry.
(B) Material Science and Future Energy
HKUST is the world leader in material and energy research. description:
The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (HKUST) established the Division of Arts ad Machine Creativity (AMC) in July 2024 under the Academy of Interdisciplinary Studies (AIS), the fifth school of HKUST. As an interdisciplinary academic unit, AMC aims to be a leading center where technology, art, and humanities converge to drive creativity and innovation. We are seeking a high-caliber academic administrator to lead this new Division as the Founding Head.
The Role
Reporting to the Dean of AIS, the Founding Head will provide leadership and manage the Division's academic and administrative functions. Key responsibilities include advancing interdisciplinary teaching and research, faculty recruitment, and resource management. The Head will also develop strategies to promote the Division and facilitate interdisciplinary collaboration within HKUST and externally with arts organizations, as well as private, governmental, and non-governmental entities.
The Candidate
Applicants should be distinguished scholars or artists with outstanding academic and/or professional accomplishments, consistent with an appointment as Full Professor with tenure or equivalent. While a background in the arts is preferred, expertise in art technology and other related areas will be considered. Prior administrative experience is highly desirable. Candidates should demonstrate proven leadership, managerial capabilities, experience in leading collaborative programs, and success in securing external funding. The ability to engage effectively with arts organizations, government, industry, and commercial sectors is advantageous.
The Division
The Division of Arts and Machine Creativity (AMC) is an interdisciplinary academic unit envisioned as a pioneering center where technology, art, and humanities drive creativity and innovation. This initiative fosters a fusion of innovation and humanities, supporting HKUST’s Strategic Plan 2031 as a major effort to expand academic frontiers through, aiming to lead positive changes in education and research, and empower the next generation to address global challenges.
The mission of the Division includes:
Bridging the gap between technology and art, by providing students and researchers with professional education and robust environment.
Cultivating artistic and creative talents equipped with the skills and knowledge to leverage emerging technologies such as AI and machine learning.
Fostering a cross-disciplinary environment that empowers collaboration and innovation among artists and technologists.
Developing cutting-edge, interdisciplinary research and education programs in partnership with other institutions in the fields of arts and machine learning
AMC’s focus areas include: (a) digital art practice (including visual, sound, performing, installation, cinematic arts); (b) machine creativity; (c) art management covering managerial, legal, and business topics related to AI arts, NFT, etc.; and (d) critical studies examining art history, media theory, and philosophy of technology in the context of arts and machine creativity. The Division will offer graduate degree programs, including MA and MFA programs, as well as MPhil/PhD programs. It will also provide common core courses for all undergraduates at HKUST, and potentially undergraduate programs in future. The Division will collaborate with the Computational Media and Arts Thrust of HKUST(GZ) to advance scientific research in artificial intelligence in generative creativity and machine creativity.
The University
Founded in 1991, HKUST is a world-renowned international research university dedicated to the advancement of learning, research, scholarship, and the education of a new generation of elite students through top-tier programs in science, engineering, business & management, humanities & social science, and interdisciplinary studies.
HKUST is deeply committed to advancing humanities and arts education and research. The School of Humanities and Social Science offers diverse music and creative writing courses led by distinguished artists and active practitioners. Courses include “Music of the World”, “Introduction to Music Composition”, and “Chinese Creative Writing”, fostering creativity and collaboration. Additionally, film courses like “Independent Cinema in Contemporary China” are offered, broadening students' artistic perspectives.
Since it was founded 33 years ago, HKUST has already established a strong presence in global higher education and received a number of international recognitions. Among others, HKUST was ranked No.3 in the Times Higher Education’s Young University Rankings 2024, 12 of its subjects were ranked among the world’s top 50 in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2024. While the University is deeply rooted in Hong Kong, HKUST (GZ) in Guangzhou, Mainland China complements the well-established disciplinary foundation at the Hong Kong campus with 4 transdisciplinary hubs and 16 thrust areas. We are dedicated to educating well-rounded students with strong entrepreneurial spirits and innovative and globally oriented thinking. English is the medium of teaching, research, and administration at HKUST. HKUST promotes diversity with an inclusive and collaborative community and the use of modern instructional methods.
Terms & Applications
The appointment will be concurrent with a substantive professorial appointment. The headship will be a full-time appointment for an initial term of three years, and renewable for another term, subject to further review. HKUST provides competitive remuneration and generous fringe benefits, including housing where appropriate.
Application, including a curriculum vitae, a vision statement, as well as names and email addresses of at least three referees, should be sent to the AMC Head Search Committee (c/o Academy of Interdisciplinary Studies), the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology, Clearwater Bay, Kowloon, Hong Kong (or by email: amcdhsearch@ust.hk ). Review of applications will begin from early December 2024 and continue until the position is filled.

description:

Postdoctoral Fellow
(Post Ref.: 26/666 )
Lingnan University is one of the eight publicly funded institutions in the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region (HKSAR) of the People’s Republic of China (PRC) and has the longest established tradition among the local institutions of higher education. It is widely recognised for providing quality education with a focus on whole-person development and conducting high-impact research for a better world. Moving forward, Lingnan University is well positioned to take lead as a comprehensive university in arts and sciences in the digital era, with impactful research and innovations.
Lingnan University offers undergraduate, taught postgraduate, and research postgraduate programmes in the Faculties of Arts, Business, Social Sciences, and the Schools of Data Science, Graduate Studies and Interdisciplinary Studies. To foster interdisciplinary collaboration and scientific progress, Lingnan University established the Lingnan University Institute for Advanced Study (LUIAS), attracting distinguished scholars from around the world to collaborate with its faculty and students. With traditional strengths in arts, business, social sciences, and interdisciplinary studies, the University aims to equip students with practical knowledge and critical thinking skills to thrive in the future. Subsequent to the establishment of the School of Data Science and LUIAS, Lingnan University is transforming into a hub for global leaders to develop and promote human-centric technology and social policies. Further information about Lingnan University is available at https://www.ln.edu.hk/ .
The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust (the Trust) has set up the Jockey Club STEM Early Career Research Fellowship for Translation and Application (formerly known as Jockey Club Global STEM Post-doctoral Fellowship for Translational Research and Application) and is now inviting applications from early career researchers from all over the world. The Fellowship will provide comprehensive support and unique opportunity to help STEM post-doctoral researchers develop their research and innovation career, expand their professional network and create social impact. The Research Grants Council (RGC) of Hong Kong is a Partner Organisation of this Fellowship.
The Fellowship
The Trust provides support for 3 years of full-time appointment for each awardee as Postdoctoral Fellow at the supporting university.
Terms and Benefits
a) a stipend of up to HK$579,200 per annum for three years, with additional 15% gratuity to be offered upon completion of the Fellowship;
b) a top-up amount of HK$10,000 per month will be provided to the appointee in addition to the basic salary;
c) academic development and exchange allowance: up to HK$32,000 per annum for three years;
d) research project seed funding: up to HK$389,000;
e) proof-of-concept ("PoC") fund: up to HK$500,000 (subject to the condition as set out in para.3 of the application guideline);
f) capacity building programmes to be offered by the Trust and its partner to enhance its translational capability, commercialisation readiness and exposure to industry and innovation ecosystems;
g) fringe benefits include annual leave, medical and dental benefits, mandatory provident fund, and incoming passage and baggage allowance for the eligible appointees.
Eligibility
Applicants should have obtained/ been conferred the first PhD degree or an equivalent qualification in Science, Technology, Engineering and Mathematics disciplines on or after 1 January 2023 ; or will complete the required qualification on or before 31 December 2026 . (If the Applicant’s conferment date is after 31 December 2026, he/she must provide supporting documents required).
Applicants must be legally permitted to work in Hong Kong.
IMPORTANT NOTE : Candidates applying for this Fellowship will not be considered by RGC for the RGC Junior Research Fellow Scheme in the same year. Shortlisted applicants will be required to attend the Commercialisation Workshop and Presentation Feedback Session arranged by the Trust.

Department of Philosophy

The Department of Philosophy at Lingnan University is one of the best in Asia. Faculty members publish in leading journals in the field, such as Analysis, Australasian Journal of Philosophy, British Journal for the Philosophy of Science, Ethics, Journal of Philosophical Logic, Mind, Noûs, Philosophers’ Imprint, Philosophical Quarterly, Philosophical Studies, Philosophy and Phenomenological Research, and Philosophy of Science. Areas of Specialization:
Philosophy of Science; Formal Epistemology; AI; or Philosophy of Biology, Chemistry, or Physics
These posts arise in connection with a Senior Research Fellowship on ‘Philosophy of Contemporary and Future Science’ awarded to Professor Darrell Rowbottom, which runs from 2022–2027. Professor Rowbottom is now seeking Two Postdoctoral Fellows to join the project team over the course of one to two years.
Details on the project, which involves scientists working with philosophers, can be found at www.pocfs.org .
We are especially interested in candidates whose work connects with the natural sciences, and especially with recent developments therein (such as increased interdisciplinarity and the involvement of AI). The teaching load will be one or two courses per year, distributed according to the departmental needs. English will be the language of instruction.

for its new Master of Social Sciences in Smart Cultural Tourism (MSSc-SCT) programme,
hosted by the Department of Sociology. The appointment will commence in September

The MSSc-SCT programme is a pioneering taught postgraduate programme in Hong Kong
that uniquely integrates cultural tourism with smart technologies. It is strategically
developed to align with the city’s vision of becoming a smart city and a cultural hub,
responding to the growing industry demand for professionals who can create in-depth,
technology-enhanced cultural experiences.

• Supervise students’ master projects and research-informed studio work.

title: 研究助理《宗族源流與弘揚：陳氏乾泰隆、黌利、元行與香港、東南亞米業及多元化企業、文化教育發展》
description:
背景
在近代香港與東南亞的華商歷史中，廣東澄海的陳氏家族寫下了跨越六代、百年不衰的商業傳奇。本研究旨在深入探討陳氏家族的宗族源流，並弘揚其從香港、泰國至整個東南亞的輝煌成就。研究將聚焦於家族始創的香港第一間南北行「乾泰隆」，由「暹羅米王」陳慈黌在泰國建立的「黌利行」，以及在新加坡開創的「元行」（初為陳生利行，後改為陳元利行），追溯其如何從傳統米業與航運，成功轉型並拓展至現代金融、保險及多元化企業的宏大歷程。
陳氏家族的發展軌跡，不僅是潮商精神的縮影，更是一個華僑家族企業如何憑藉世代傳承的智慧與開拓精神，在不同時代背景下順應時勢、銳意革新，並持續為所在地區經濟、社會及文化作出卓越貢獻的典範。本研究將透過系統性的梳理與訪談，撰寫《宗族源流與弘揚》一書，使大眾更深刻地認識陳氏家族對香港、東南亞乃至全球華商網絡的深遠影響。
工作職責
檔案館與圖書館調研： 前往各大政府檔案處（如香港歷史檔案館）、大學圖書館、博物館或民間機構，實地收集、掃描、影印相關歷史檔案與文獻。
數字化與數據庫檢索： 利用各類中英文數字學術數據庫（如近代中國史料數據庫、地方志、報紙數據庫等）進行關鍵詞檢索。
文獻綜述： 閱讀、整理和歸納與研究課題相關的已有學術成果，撰寫文獻綜述以支持研究框架。
錄音轉錄與口述歷史整理： 如果項目涉及「口述歷史」，需協助準備訪談提綱，並將訪談錄音逐字轉錄為文字稿，進行校對與整理。
會議協調： 安排研究小組會議，記錄會議摘要，並跟進後續待辦事項。
職位要求
歷史學學士畢業，有碩士學位為佳。
一年以上歷史學研究經驗。
曾有進行一年以上研究項目，曾出刊學術論文，曾籌辦學術研討會。

description:
Chu Hai College has provided 78 years of quality education and excellence to the Hong Kong community and remains committed to enhancing educational opportunities for young people. Its purpose and vision are to nurture future leaders, strengthen the competitiveness of Hong Kong, and help bring about a stable, prosperous and harmonious society in a knowledge-based economy.
Academic departments within the College include Chinese Literature, English, Journalism and Communication, Business Administration, Accounting and Banking, Finance, Computer Science, Civil Engineering, and Architecture. The Faculty of Business comprises three departments, offering programmes to meet the needs for both hard and soft skills in the business world, and to strengthen the ethical sense of our future business leaders.
The College is registered as an Approved Post Secondary College under the Post Secondary Colleges Ordinance (Cap 320), with all degree programmes accredited by the Hong Kong Council for Accreditation of Academic and Vocational Qualifications (HKCAAVQ).
The Dean of Faculty of Business is responsible for providing overall effective leadership in the management and development of the Faculty, the development of appropriate programmes in response to community needs, the smooth operation of programmes, the conduct of good quality teaching and learning activities, the promotion of research and scholarship and the establishment of partnerships with various external stakeholders in the Government, the academic profession and the industry.
REQUIREMENTS
The ideal candidate is expected to possess:
1. a Doctoral degree or equivalent;
2. proficiency in Chinese and English;
3. a demonstrated record of excellence in teaching, research and service commensurate with that of an associate professor, in disciplines of Business;
4. experience in serving in prestigious higher education institution(s) preferably at the rank of Faculty/ School Dean or above level;
5. abundant experience in providing effective leadership to Faculties or academic units with regard to disciplines of Business, including overseeing the development of academic strategy and its implementation; academic budget planning and allocation; personnel management; grants submission processes and management; and student enrollment
MAJOR DUTIES & RESPONSIBILITIES
The Dean, Faculty of Business shall:
1. be responsible for the management of the Faculty of Business and shall exercise the responsibilities of Faculty Dean in accordance as required.
2. provide visionary leadership and direction for the Faculty of Business, including formulating annual development plans and budget for the Faculty in accordance with the College practices.
3. lead the curriculum development as well as initiation and development of new undergraduate and postgraduate programmes in line with the College's Vision and Missions and Strategic Plan.
4. encourage high standards of teaching, foster and encourage research within the Faculty of Business.
5. establish and maintain connections with other academic institutions, professional bodies and industry, both local and international.
6. oversee staff management and accountability in the Faculty of Business.
APPLICATION
Applicants are invited to send their detailed curriculum vitae, including current and expected salary, and direct any enquiries to the Human Resources Office, Hong Kong Chu Hai College [E-mail: recruitment@chuhai.edu.hk ], quoting the position being applied for and the reference number. Recruitment will continue until the position is filled. Candidature may be obtained by nominations. The College reserves the right to make an appointment by invitation or not to fill this post.
